source.title: Sparse Attention Tradeoffs
source.text: Sparse Attention Tradeoffs. In a controlled 64k-token benchmark, block-sparse attention reduced peak memory use by 37 percent and improved throughput by 22 percent compared with full attention. Accuracy on long-range retrieval fell by 2 percentage points. The study used one synthetic scientific corpus, so the authors caution that the efficiency gains may not generalize to other domains.
